Weddings

A wedding here is a Sunday on a farm that has been in one family for four generations. The ceremony is in the field facing Pleasant Mountain, the reception is in the barn, and the two of you get ready in the ell. We host up to 135 guests, May through October.

How a day works here

  1. Get ready in the ell

    The bridal room and the groom’s room are steps from the barn, each with a mirror and a place to sit.

  2. Ceremony in the field

    Benches made from the barn’s old floorboards, facing Pleasant Mountain. On a wet day, the ceremony moves into the barn.

  3. Reception in the barn

    Dinner on the main floor and in the loft, dancing under the original beams, your caterer in the prep kitchen.

  4. Sunset on the patio

    String lights, the stone seating circle, and the view down the field as the light goes.

Why Sundays

We keep Saturday as our day of rest, so our weddings are on Sundays. A Sunday wedding also means a quieter weekend for your guests, and most vendors have the date open. [CONFIRM: wording Susan is comfortable with]

Questions couples ask

How many guests can the barn hold?

135. That is the capacity on our town permit for any event.

Can we have our ceremony outside?

Yes. The ceremony field faces Pleasant Mountain, with benches made from the barn’s old floorboards. In rain, the ceremony moves into the barn.

Can we bring our own caterer?

Yes. There is a prep kitchen with barn doors your caterer can close while they finish the meal.

Can we serve alcohol?

No. We are an alcohol-free venue, and that is part of our town permit. Many couples tell us it makes for a family day.

Do you host Saturday weddings?

No. Our weddings are on Sundays, and we also book weekdays.

What months are you open?

May through October. October is our favorite.

Are tables and chairs included?

Yes. 6-foot and 8-foot tables, 5-foot rounds, and chairs for the ceremony and the reception.

Is the barn accessible?

Yes. There are three accessible parking spaces in the driveway, a wooden ramp to the main floor, an ADA accessible bathroom, and a paved path around the barn to the patio.

How do we book?

Email or text Susan to schedule a tour. After the tour we send the contract and the pricing brochure. [CONFIRM: deposit and booking steps]
